extracted.intended_audience: people writing press releases (PR professionals, small-business owners, startup founders, communications staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step practical guidance for preparing, writing, reviewing, and distributing news-style press releases that are concise, newsworthy, and media-ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify a newsworthy story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select an angle that reporters and audiences will care about — demonstrable change, timeliness, relevance, impact. If it isn't inherently newsworthy, reconsider issuing a release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your target audience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be clear which audience(s) the release is for (trade, local, national, consumers) and shape tone, details, and distribution list accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research relevant journalists
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify reporters and outlets that cover the topic; personalize outreach rather than blasting an untargeted list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather all key facts and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather all key facts and approvals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect verified facts, figures, names, dates, and secure any necessary internal approvals before distribution to avoid retractions or edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare multimedia assets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include high-quality images, video, charts or other assets to increase pickup; ensure files are properly captioned and available via links or attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with the most important news (headline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead with the most important news
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The headline should prioritize the single most newsworthy element to grab attention immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use active voice (headline)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer active constructions in the headline to be direct and engaging; avoid passive phrasing that buries the subject or action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep headline under 80 characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for succinctness to improve readability and fit in email subject lines and social shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid clichés in headline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of overused buzzwords that weaken credibility; use specific claims backed by evidence instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test headline with 'would I tweet this?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the headline isn't shareable or interesting in a short social message, revise it for clarity and appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compress 5 W's into 50 words (lede)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lede should succinctly answer who, what, when, where, why (and how if relevant) in about 50 words to deliver the core news quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with the most newsworthy element (lede)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the strongest, most newsworthy detail first in the lede rather than background or boilerplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include concrete details in lede
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific figures, named sources, and precise dates to give credibility and allow reporters to act on the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid throat-clearing in lede
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skip formulaic opener phrases that waste space; get to the news immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active voice throughout (lede/body)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain active constructions across lede and body for clarity and energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use inverted pyramid (body)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the body so the most critical information appears first and supporting/contextual details follow; this helps editors trim without losing the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: One idea per paragraph
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep paragraphs short and focused so readers and journalists can quickly scan and extract facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a quote on first page
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a quote on first page
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide at least one attributed quote early to humanize the story and offer a reporter a ready soundbite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide methodology if data-based
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the release cites research or data, include brief methodological details so reporters can evaluate credibility and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep body to 3-4 paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for brevity — a compact body is more likely to be read and used by journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote length guideline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep quoted material concise (roughly 25–35 words) so it functions as a clear, quotable soundbite rather than long exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should feel authentic and conversational, avoiding corporate-speak that reporters may discard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote should add information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should provide perspective, context, or a new fact rather than restating what's already in the headline or lede.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unproven superlatives in quotes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use unsubstantiated claims like "best" or "industry-leading" unless you can back them up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute quote to a named C-level executive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the full name and title (e.g., CEO, CMO) to add authority and ease reporter attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate length guideline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the boilerplate concise (about 50–75 words) summarizing founding, headquarters, mission and core facts for background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate content requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The boilerplate should include founding date, headquarters location, and a one-line mission/what-the-company-does statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named media contact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a specific contact person (name and title) so journalists know who to call for follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct phone number
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a direct phone number (not a general switchboard) to enable quick reporter contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct email
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an email address for the media contact to facilitate electronic follow-up and requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: End with '###' marker
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude the release with the industry-standard "###" to signal the end of content to editors and wire services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have outside reader review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get an external reviewer to catch unclear phrasing, factual gaps, or errors a writer might miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify all facts and numbers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check figures, dates, names, and claims; incorrect facts reduce credibility and can cause the story to be killed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check spelling of names
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct spelling of people, company names, and partner organizations to avoid offense and retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test all links
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that URLs and downloadable assets work and point to the intended resources before distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribute to relevant journalists
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send the release to targeted reporters/editors who cover the beat rather than a generic mass list; tailor pitch where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire syndication for SEO
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider wire services to increase online visibility and search engine presence, but weigh against the need for targeted outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid burying the lede
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not hide the main news deep in the body; place it up front in the headline and lede.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using too many adjectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Using too many adjectives (mistake to avoid)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit flowery modifiers; prefer concrete facts and evidence over promotional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid quotes that say nothing
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote that says nothing (mistake to avoid)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure quotes add perspective or new information; avoid hollow or formulaic statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid boilerplate that's too long
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep background concise; overly long boilerplates dilute the release's utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include multimedia (don't omit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of images/video reduces pickup; include ready-to-use assets whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mass-blast distribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sending irrelevant mass emails harms media relationships and reduces chances of coverage; prefer targeted pitches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sending on Friday afternoon
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing matters — avoid low-engagement windows like late Friday when newsrooms may be understaffed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid following up too aggressively
rubrics_metrics.description: Following up too aggressively (mistake to avoid)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect reporters' time; follow up politely and sparingly rather than frequent persistent messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthy substance (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release must have genuine news value — a substantive announcement or data point that matters to the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active voice headline under 80 chars (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines headline rules: be active and concise to maximize clarity and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 50-word lede with 5 W's (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compact lede that answers who/what/when/where/why in roughly 50 words scores highly for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverted pyramid body (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize information so the most important facts appear first, enabling easy editing and rapid comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: 25-35 word substantive quote (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short, informative quote that adds perspective and is easily excerpted is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: 75-word boilerplate (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The quality rubric lists ~75 words as a target for the boilerplate; keep it succinct while including key background facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named contact with phone (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a specific media contact and direct phone number to facilitate reporter follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outside reviewer used (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having an external reviewer is part of the quality checklist to catch errors and improve clarity.
